title: Boss: the access log report
summary: A ticket from the SRE team: parse the web server's access log, anonymise client IPs, find a tracing bug and read request tags, all with groups.

steps.title: The ticket
body: **OPS-482: weekly access report.** The edge proxy writes the Common Log Format (CLF), the default of many web servers:
Client IP, two unused fields, the time in brackets, the request in quotes, the status and the bytes sent (`-` when
nothing was sent). The ticket asks for:
1. A pattern that splits a line into named fields.
2. A C# parser that turns a line into a record.
3. Anonymised client IPs before the logs are shared with a vendor (privacy review).
4. A filter for a tracing bug: spans that name themselves as their own parent.
5. The request tags, which are a repeated list.
Read every field by name. The pattern will change next quarter, and the report must not.

steps.title: Split an access log line
prompt: Match a **whole** access log line with named groups `ip`, `time` (what is inside the brackets), `method`, `path`,
`status` and `bytes` (digits, or a single `-`). The protocol (`HTTP/1.1`, `HTTP/2.0`) is matched but not captured.
IPv4 addresses only.

steps.title: Parse it into a record
prompt: Write `AccessEntry? ParseAccess(string line)`. Return `null` when the line does not fit the whole format. When
`bytes` is `-`, the record holds `0`. The record is already declared:
```csharp
record AccessEntry(string Ip, string Method, string Path, int Status, long Bytes);
Read every group by name. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("a GET line", new AccessEntry("203.0.113.7", "GET", "/api/orders/42", 200, 512), ParseAccess("203.0.113.7 - - [26/Nov/2026:09:12:04 +0000] \"GET /api/orders/42 HTTP/1.1\" 200 512"));
Dojo.Eq("bytes '-' becomes 0", new AccessEntry("198.51.100.23", "POST", "/api/pay", 503, 0), ParseAccess("198.51.100.23 - - [26/Nov/2026:09:12:05 +0000] \"POST /api/pay HTTP/2.0\" 503 -"));
Dojo.Eq("a query string stays in the path", new AccessEntry("10.0.0.4", "GET", "/search?q=a", 304, 0), ParseAccess("10.0.0.4 - - [26/Nov/2026:09:13:00 +0000] \"GET /search?q=a HTTP/1.1\" 304 0"));
Dojo.Eq("a large response", new AccessEntry("10.0.0.4", "GET", "/export", 200, 5000000000), ParseAccess("10.0.0.4 - - [26/Nov/2026:09:14:00 +0000] \"GET /export HTTP/1.1\" 200 5000000000"));
Dojo.Eq("a garbled line gives null", (AccessEntry?)null, ParseAccess("203.0.113.7 GET /api/orders/42 200"));
Dojo.Eq("trailing junk gives null", (AccessEntry?)null, ParseAccess("10.0.0.4 - - [26/Nov/2026:09:13:00 +0000] \"GET / HTTP/1.1\" 200 12 extra"));
record AccessEntry(string Ip, string Method, string Path, int Status, long Bytes);

forbid.message: Reads groups by name, not by number

steps.title: Anonymise client IPs
prompt: Before the logs go to the vendor, replace the last part of every IPv4 address with `0`: `203.0.113.7` becomes
`203.0.113.0`. Capture the first three parts in a group (name it `net`) and write the replacement. A version
number like `1.2.3` has only three parts and must stay as it is.

steps.title: Find spans that are their own parent
prompt: **Symptom.** The tracing UI hangs on some requests. The cause is a bug in one client library that sometimes
writes a span whose `parent` is its own `span` id, so the tree has a loop.
Lines look like `op=GET span=a1b2 parent=c3d4 ms=3` (ids are lowercase hex; `span` always comes before `parent`).
Find the lines where `parent` is the **same id** as `span`. `parent=a1b2c` is a different id from `a1b2`.

steps.title: Read the request tags
prompt: Some lines carry tags: `user=ada tags=api;prod;eu-west latency=12`. Tags are letters, digits, `_` and `-`,
separated by `;`.
Write `List<string> Tags(string line)` that returns the tags in order, or an empty list when there is no `tags=`
field (`pretags=x` is not a tags field). Use **one** regex with a repeated named group and read every repetition
from `Group.Captures` (no `Split`). `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("three tags in order", new List<string> { "api", "prod", "eu-west" }, Tags("user=ada tags=api;prod;eu-west latency=12"));
Dojo.Eq("a single tag", new List<string> { "solo" }, Tags("tags=solo"));
Dojo.Eq("no tags field", new List<string>(), Tags("user=ada latency=12"));
Dojo.Eq("pretags is not a tags field", new List<string>(), Tags("pretags=x"));

forbid.message: Does not split the string: one regex does it all
